edges.effect_quant: Across randomized and pooled evidence, eradication of H. pylori consistently lowers future gastric cancer incidence, with the strongest benefit when treatment occurs before advanced premalignant change and with some meta-analyses also showing lower gastric-cancer mortality.
edges.population: H. pylori-positive adults, particularly in higher-incidence populations, treated with eradication therapy for primary gastric cancer prevention
edges.mechanism: Eradication removes the chronic inflammatory and mutagenic stimulus driving the Correa cascade from chronic gastritis toward atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and eventually gastric adenocarcinoma.
edges.summary: This is one of the cleaner prevention edges in gastrointestinal oncology. The protective signal is reproducible across randomized trials and meta-analyses, even though the magnitude varies and late-stage premalignant lesions appear less modifiable than earlier disease.
edges.caveats: Most randomized evidence comes from East Asian populations with relatively high baseline gastric cancer risk, so absolute benefit will vary by region and baseline incidence. The preventive effect is smaller once intestinal metaplasia or dysplasia is already established.

evidence.notes: Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy to prevent gastric cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: gastric cancer incidence after eradication therapy versus placebo or no treatment in healthy infected adults

evidence.citation: Rokkas T et al 2017 Ann Gastroenterol
evidence.notes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the role of Helicobacter pylori eradication in preventing gastric cancer.

effect_quant.comparator: gastric cancer risk in successfully eradicated patients versus controls
